short: This entry holds the HMG-box factors that are neither SOX nor TCF/LEF: HMG20A (iBRAF), HMG20B (BRAF35) and BBX (bobby sox homolog). They share only the fold. HMG20A and HMG20B are paralogous subunits of chromatin complexes - HMG20B of the LSD1-CoREST-HDAC complex that keeps neuronal genes off in non-neuronal cells, HMG20A of KMT2A/MLL complexes that turn them on - so their genomic distribution is largely set by whichever partner recruits the complex. BBX is a poorly characterized protein that groups phylogenetically with CIC rather than with SOX. The three measured motifs are unrelated to each other and to the SOX core, and this is the least coherent family in the HMG class; a hit here should be treated as a lead, not an identification.
long:
## The factors

Three proteins are collected here, and what they have in common is a single HMG box, not a site.
HMG20B, originally named BRAF35 (BRCA2-associated factor 35), is a core subunit of the BHC
complex that pairs LSD1 (KDM1A) and CoREST with histone deacetylases and represses neuronal
genes in non-neuronal cells [PMID:12032298]. HMG20A, its paralogue, was named iBRAF for inhibitor of BRAF35: it
opposes that complex and instead recruits KMT2A/MLL to drive neuronal gene expression [PMID:16227968], and it is
also found in a KMT2A-associated PHF5A-PHF14-HMG20A-RAI1 subcomplex [PMID:37709746]. HMG20B has a separate
mitotic function that depends on its interaction with the BRC repeats of BRCA2 [PMID:21399666]. Both are broadly
expressed. BBX is a larger, much less studied protein, broadly expressed with enrichment in the
central nervous system, which phylogenetic analysis places with CIC (capicua) in an HMG-box
subfamily distinct from both SOX and TCF/LEF [PMID:25079045]. The important structural point is that most HMG
boxes are architectural rather than sequence-reading domains: the HMGB1/HMGB2 type binds and
bends DNA with little sequence preference, and only a minority of the superfamily - SOX,
TCF/LEF, CIC and a few others - has demonstrable sequence specificity [PMID:7774012]. Nothing published
establishes that HMG20A or HMG20B selects a specific sequence in cells.

## The motif

There is no single consensus for this family, which is why none is given. The four models here
disagree with each other; cohesion is 0.45, the lowest of the HMG-class families. BBX gives the
most informative model, and it is the family medoid: CIS-BP reports TGAACRVCGTTCA (15.1 bits), the human HT-SELEX matrix of Yin et al. 2017,
and the Vierstra archetype AC0363 reports TGAACRNYGTTCA (15.8 bits) [PMID:25215497,28473536,32728250]. These are the same 13-base element - an inverted repeat, since TGAAC and GTTCA are reverse complements, with three variable bases between them - but not two measurements of it: Vierstra archetypes are clusters of models compiled from existing collections [PMID:32728250], so AC0363 most likely re-renders the same in vitro data. The half-site resembles the TGAAT half of the dimeric,
palindromic sites that appear in SOX models (Vierstra TGAATGTGCAGTCA, HOCOMOCO SOX1
TGAATANCATTCAT), differing at one position, which is consistent with BBX reading DNA in the same
general way as other sequence-specific HMG boxes. HMG20A's single HOCOMOCO model,
HM20A.H14CORE.0.SB.A, reads TCCCTAGGC (11.5 bits); its fourth field carries S, so it rests on
HT-SELEX rather than on ChIP, and it is graded A. CCTAGG is itself palindromic but bears no
relation to the SOX or TCF/LEF core. The HMG20B model, CIS-BP M02487_2.00, is ATTATAT (10.5
bits) and is inferred from the mouse protein at 94% DNA-binding-domain identity [PMID:25215497]; a short AT-rich
string of this kind is what a non-sequence-specific HMG box tends to produce in a selection
experiment, and it should not be read as a recognition sequence.

## Where it acts

For HMG20A and HMG20B the practical answer is: wherever the complex goes. LSD1-CoREST-HDAC is
recruited to neuronal gene promoters largely by REST binding its own RE1/NRSE element [PMID:12032298], and KMT2A
complexes are recruited by their own targeting subunits; HMG20A and HMG20B come along as
subunits. Locations reported for them therefore track partner occupancy - neuronal gene
promoters, pancreatic islet regulatory regions where HMG20A is required for beta cell
maturation [PMID:29449530], adipocyte loci where HMG20A acts through MEF2C [PMID:36142473], and KMT2A targets in pancreatic
cancer stem cells [PMID:37709746]. BBX has been mapped less. Its 13-base palindrome is specific by the standards
of this atlas: with two degenerate inner positions, TGAACRVCGTTCA is expected only a few hundred
times in a 3.1 Gb genome, against tens of thousands for the nine-base HMG20A model and millions
for a bare six-base HMG core.

## Biology and disease

HMG20B is required for repression of the neuronal program in non-neuronal cells and for
completion of mitosis [PMID:12032298,21399666], and its splicing has been implicated in breast cancer [PMID:39731153]; the HMG20A locus
is a genome-wide-association signal for type 2 diabetes, and HMG20A is needed for functional
maturity of pancreatic beta cells [PMID:29449530], restrains adipogenesis through MEF2C [PMID:36142473], and supports the stem-
cell state in pancreatic cancer. The HMG20A/HMG20B antagonism is a clean example of two
paralogues with the same DNA-binding domain having opposite effects by virtue of the complexes
they join. BBX has been linked to phosphate homeostasis through regulation of FGF23 in bone [PMID:39482539], and
is maternally expressed and CNS-enriched in zebrafish and mouse [PMID:25079045]. None of the three has an
established monogenic human disease.

## Reading a hit

Treat this family as a fold, not a motif: the models do not resemble one another and the family
cohesion is 0.45. The BBX palindrome is worth taking seriously as a sequence - it is long enough to be rare - but its presence in two databases is not independent confirmation, and the label rests on in vitro selection with no structural or functional follow-up, so "BBX site" is provisional, and because
the half-sites resemble those of dimeric SOX sites you should exclude SOX before settling on
BBX. An HMG20A match does not license the conclusion that HMG20A occupies the site: the HT-SELEX
evidence supports "this protein can bind this sequence", while in cells HMG20A is a passenger in
LSD1-CoREST and KMT2A complexes whose distribution is set by REST and other partners, so check
for an RE1/NRSE element nearby. The HMG20B model is mouse-inferred and low in information; do
not use it to call sites. More generally, a weak AT-rich match labelled with an HMG-box protein
is more likely to reflect a shape preference than a recognition sequence.
caveats: Low confidence throughout. This is a fold-defined group with no shared consensus and the lowest cohesion in the HMG class (0.45) across only four models. The BBX 13-base palindrome appears in two databases that most likely share one in vitro source, so they do not confirm each other; it is rare enough to be useful, but rests on in vitro selection alone and its half-sites overlap those of dimeric SOX sites. The HMG20A motif has HT-SELEX support, yet HMG20A acts as a subunit of LSD1-CoREST and KMT2A complexes, so genomic locations attributed to it may belong to REST or another recruiting factor. The HMG20B model is inferred from mouse at 94% DNA-binding-domain identity and is an uninformative AT-rich string.

timeline.finding: BRAF35 (HMG20B) is purified as a subunit of the BHC complex, which joins LSD1 and CoREST to histone deacetylases and is recruited by REST to the RE1/NRSE element of neuronal genes; a point mutation in the BRAF35 HMG domain blocks REST-mediated repression.
timeline.methods: Complex purification and mass spectrometry, chromatin immunoprecipitation, reporter assays
timeline.open: The HMG domain mattered for repression, but no sequence preference was defined for BRAF35 itself.

timeline.finding: HMG20A, named iBRAF, is shown to antagonize BRAF35: it accumulates at neuronal gene promoters during differentiation, recruits the methyltransferase MLL and raises H3K4 trimethylation, activating the genes BRAF35 helps repress.
timeline.methods: Chromatin immunoprecipitation, knockdown and overexpression in P19 cells

timeline.finding: HMG20B acquires a function unrelated to transcription: it binds the BRC5 repeat of BRCA2, and its depletion blocks completion of cell division.
timeline.methods: RNA interference, in vitro binding, peptide competition

timeline.finding: HT-SELEX of human BBX gives a 13-base palindrome, TGAACGCCGTTCA, the only informative model in this group; the CIS-BP BBX model (TGAACRVCGTTCA) is the same matrix. A 2014 phylogenetic analysis had already placed BBX with CIC in an HMG-box subfamily separate from SOX and TCF/LEF.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX (as compiled in JASPAR and CIS-BP); earlier phylogenetics and expression analysis
timeline.open: No structure, no genomic occupancy data and no functional test of the proposed BBX site.

timeline.finding: HMG20A is linked to beta cell biology: it is expressed in human and mouse islets, reduced in islets from type 2 diabetic donors, needed for glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, and the diabetes-associated rs7119 variant lowers its expression in a reporter assay.
timeline.methods: Expression profiling, knockdown in islets and cell lines, chromatin immunoprecipitation, reporter assays

timeline.finding: Clustering human motif collections into archetypes keeps the BBX palindrome as its own archetype, AC0363, rather than folding it into the SOX or TCF/LEF clusters, which is the strongest evidence that it is a distinct element.
timeline.open: Archetypes are clustered from the same motif collections, so this is not an independent measurement of the BBX site.

timeline.finding: HMG20A is found in a PHF5A-PHF14-HMG20A-RAI1 subcomplex that binds the histone methyltransferase KMT2A in pancreatic cancer stem cells, reinforcing the picture of HMG20A as a complex subunit rather than a site-selecting factor.
timeline.methods: Proteomics, chromatin profiling, inhibitor and xenograft experiments

timeline.finding: The first mammalian loss-of-function phenotype for BBX: Bbx-null and osteocyte-specific Bbx-deleted mice have raised serum FGF23, low serum phosphate and reduced bone mass, and BBX suppresses vitamin D-induced Fgf23 promoter activity.
timeline.methods: Mouse knockouts, serum chemistry, promoter and interaction assays
timeline.open: Whether BBX acts at the Fgf23 promoter through its own palindromic site or through its interaction with the vitamin D receptor was not resolved.

open: Whether HMG20A and HMG20B select DNA sequences in cells at all is unresolved: HT-SELEX gives HMG20A a grade-A model for TCCCTAGGC, yet both proteins are documented as subunits of LSD1-CoREST and KMT2A complexes whose placement is set by REST and other targeting factors, and no ChIP-derived motif exists for either.

How BBX represses FGF23 is open: the mouse work shows both a vitamin D receptor interaction with ubiquitin-dependent BBX degradation and an effect on Fgf23 promoter activity, without establishing whether a BBX site in that promoter is occupied.
